blind_comparisons.not_possible_reason: The item's own method makes its blind pass conditional: 'using RI-VIS02 REF-M6 as the reference if and only if a usable reference image exists; otherwise record the pair as skipped'. REF-M6 (modern/character_closeup/REF-M6__rdr2-horseshoe-overlook-camp.jpg) is a mid-distance rear view; our matched artefact is a close-up at >= 40% frame height. A pack built from these two would measure the framing difference, not the fidelity.

The item declares blind_pair: no by construction — it forbids a modern design target under CC-2, and Morrowind's characters are a fidelity mismatch so gross that a judge would be answering 'which is higher resolution'.

score.band_label: ART 1/10 x FIDELITY 3/10 — an ordered pair, never averaged (CC-5). The rig is sound; the surface hung on it is not built.
score.aggregation_note: min, because RI-VIS01 §E gates the wave on min(ART, FIDELITY) and these two items are gates on disjoint axes rather than two dimensions of one thing. The pair is the real result; the scalar exists only for the progress page.

status_reasons: ART 1/10 is below the wave-1 gate of 7.0 and below RI-VIS10's own <6 wave-blocking threshold.
FIDELITY 3/10 is below the wave-1 gate of 7.0 and below RI-VIS08's own <6 wave-blocking threshold.
Three of RI-VIS10's five top tells are present: a human with a lizard head, everyone is the same man, and brand-new clothes on a poor province.

biggest_gap.what: The visible body of every character in the game is an assembly of primitive solids rather than a built figure, and the numbers say so on both axes at once. Shoulders are glossy ellipsoids attached to a flat rectangular torso plate; the pelvis is a trapezoid; limbs are tapered cones; the player's legs terminate in points with no foot. The face carries 1 of 7 landmarks (a crest root, and nothing else — no brow ridge, orbit rim, naris, cheek-to-jaw line, mandible line or chin underside). The whole shipped roster is 5.87-6.84 heads tall (median 6.58) against RI-VIS10 C1's 7.0-8.0 band, with 0 of 41 figures inside it. The player is 15142 triangles against RI-VIS08 B2's 25000 and the creature 4834 against 12000. The skin opens 289 crack pixels across 179 of 640 posed frames at the calf/foot and head/hand seams. The art family that carries 329 of 408 NPCs has no eye geometry at all. Crucially this is NOT a rig defect: the same build passes RI-VIS08 C1, C3, C4, C6, C7, C8 and C9 with foot slide at 6 mm against a 30 mm bar, root-motion r = 1.0000, grip error 0.000 m and foot IK holding 100% of planted frames on a 20-degree slope and on stairs.
biggest_gap.why_it_matters: It is the reason the owner, playing the game, said the player character and every NPC look frankly ridiculous — a viewer identifies an ellipsoid stuck to a slab in the first half-second, before texture, light or animation is considered at all.

remedy.action: Rebuild the visible character surface on the existing skeleton — do not touch the rig, the clips or the IK, which measure well. In game/src/render/actor.js: (1) replace the ellipsoid-shoulder / slab-torso construction with a continuous shoulder-to-chest surface and tapered limbs, and give the player a foot; (2) add the facial landmark geometry — brow ridge, orbit rim, naris, cheek-to-jaw line, mandible line, chin underside — to both base.saxhleel and base.humanoid, and give base.humanoid the eye and pupil parts base.saxhleel already has; (3) change the per-family head scale in CHARACTER_SPECS so the head-count canon lands in band.
remedy.acceptance: node tools/visual/f10-silhouette.mjs --res=768 --pose=idle_loop reports >= 90% of shipped figures with R inside 7.0-8.0 (6.5-7.5 for naga and orsimer) and none outside 6.0-8.5; RI-VIS08 B2 reports >= 25000 triangles for the player and >= 12000 for the beast family; RI-VIS10 B4 counts >= 5 of 7 facial landmarks producing visible form shading under a 45-degree key; RI-VIS08 B8 passes on every art family, not only saxhleel; node tools/visual/actor-orbit-holes.mjs --res=512 --angles=8 --distances=4 reports 0 crack pixels.

secondary_observations: CHEAPEST HIGH-VALUE FIX, and it is one predicate: game/src/render/renderer.js:693 selects the art family with (n.race==='saxhleel'||n.race==='naga')?'saxhleel':'humanoid'. The string 'argonian' carries 181 of 408 NPC records — 44.4% of the roster, and the actual reptilian race of Black Marsh — and is not in that test, so those NPCs render on base.humanoid: no snout, no crest, no horn, no eyes. 329 of 408 NPCs land on that family in total. This is the mechanical cause of RI-VIS10 C2's IoU 1.0000 pairs (an argonian rootkeeper and a breton mudborn are pixel-identical) and of E5 failing. It is not the biggest gap because fixing it alone leaves the player — already on the saxhleel family — exactly as it is, and the owner named the player first.
The 12 race strings in use include 'none' and 'mixed', and 'argonian' is not among the 10 ids declared in game/data/progression/races.json. The data and the declaration have drifted apart.

NPC placement: subject npc-lilmoth-apothecary-12 (Ixtei, an apothecary) stands in open water off the Lilmoth pier — all 17 of her frames are sea and sky. Two further NPCs in C4__npc-dockmaster-weeja-sen__yaw000.png stand waist-deep in water with their feet below the jetty deck.
The Lilmoth plaza at the char-player stand held no NPC on screen in any of the four wide frames, which is why RI-VIS10 E4 could not be demonstrated either way.

RI-VIS08 C7 measures grip_err at 0.000 m, so the sword that crosses the player's entire silhouette at 90 and 180 degrees is not an attachment bug — it is a weapon-scale art decision, and it belongs to the weapons piece rather than to F10.

My own capture tool reported '0 red' for 17 frames that contain no subject at all. A tool that cannot distinguish an empty frame from a full one will certify an absence as a capture; tools/visual/f10-character-sweep.mjs needs a subject-coverage assertion before it is reused.

corpus_extended.what: B3's hard fail now reads 'texture-only OR ABSENT' for crest, snout and tail, and its pass condition says an absent feature does not satisfy that arm.
corpus_extended.why: B3 scored only features 'scored present in B2', so an absent feature was removed from its denominator and could not fail it. This build has no tail geometry at all and therefore PASSED B3 — the single design check it passed — while failing B2 at 3/10. The item's own §F#1 calls a species asserted rather than built the cardinal sin; absent is a worse instance of it than painted, yet scored better.
corpus_extended.self_serving_check: Re-applied to this verdict it turns B3 from PASS to FAIL and moves DESIGN from 3/18 to 2/18. The amendment makes the amending critic's own piece worse, which is the test that it is not self-serving. It is not the reason any piece passes anything.

method_deviations.what: RI-VIS10 B1, C4 and D4 require a fresh judge with no answer key. None could be obtained: RULES.md rule 0 records create_session as approval-gated (MCP error -32003) and rule 25 forbids judging a pack I built.
method_deviations.why: Scored FAIL under the item's own rule that an unpublished census fails its check rather than being removed. The B1 <40% cap-at-4 was NOT applied, because that requires a measurement I do not have.

method_deviations.what: RI-VIS10 C1 and C2 were measured on an offline orthographic rasterisation of the shipped actor rather than on an in-game frame.
method_deviations.why: The item requires published pixel numbers reproducible by a second critic and pairwise IoU over binary masks. An in-game frame has a world behind the figure and no ID buffer is exposed, so segmenting one would be a guess; a perspective camera would also make R depend on the distance the critic happened to choose. The rasteriser reproduces the game's own family selection (from race) and variant selection (from the npc:<eid> hash), and makes no colour, material or light claim.

method_deviations.what: RI-VIS08 B1, B3, B4, B5 and B6 were not computed.
method_deviations.why: B6 was never captured (no backlit setup — the critic's omission). B1, B3, B4 and B5 have their hardware frames in hand but the pixel statistics were not run within this pass. All five scored 0 fail-closed per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §7.3, and all five are recorded as owed for the next round rather than absorbed into the build's score.

method_deviations.what: Two RunPod attempts failed before any frame was taken, with the Pod agent returning HTTP 404 on GET /job within 250 ms of submission.
method_deviations.why: Recorded rather than hidden. Both Pods were terminated and deletion confirmed by API lookup. The third attempt succeeded and produced all 93 hardware frames.

self_audit.self_audit_note: ran_every_assigned_method is false. RI-VIS08 B1/B3/B4/B5/B6 were not computed and RI-VIS10 B1/C4/D4 could not obtain a fresh judge; every one is scored 0 or FAIL fail-closed per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §7.3 and SCORING.md §1.1, none omitted and none averaged away. The escalation ladder was applied and did not need to be: the gap was found at step 1 (put our capture beside the plate and look) and was then confirmed at higher zoom (the offline rasteriser at 768 px), on a changed sample (five subjects across two art families rather than the player alone), and on a second-order property (silhouette IoU across the roster rather than 'is there a character').

notes: The gap ledger for these subsystem paths was read only AFTER raw measurement was complete, per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §8. The recorded prior scores (RI-VIS08 3/10, RI-CAM07 4/10) were treated as claims to attack rather than inherit: RI-VIS08 lands at 3 again, but for the first time with a measured basis — a full five-scenario §A trace, a triangle census and a part census — rather than an impression, and the DYNAMIC half of it is now known to be at 7/10 rather than uniformly poor. One claim I made mid-pass was wrong and is withdrawn in the markdown §0.5: I reported two M1 reference videos missing from disk after reading a truncated `ls | head`; re-run, refs/video/ holds 10 files and a walk of the generated set finds 254 routed members with 0 missing. Two defects in the reference set itself are filed in markdown §8: one of the four D1 ESO plates depicts a human woman in a hat rather than an Argonian, and the C4 full-body plates are headless armour item renders, which means RI-VIS10 C1's head-count canon has no reference side to be compared against at all. One corpus amendment was filed mid-pass and is declared in corpus_extended: RI-VIS10 B3's absent-feature seam, tightened. Three further findings are recorded in the markdown §8 as data defects in refs/characters/ and a return-value mismatch in anim-metrics.mjs, and are deliberately NOT built inside this critique per CRITIC-DOCTRINE §1.3's bounding guard.
